A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CycleQD research work, with all 21 pages and Appendices A and B available. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the scientific content matches completely.

before.justification: v2 reports original computer-science experiments, ablations, generalization evaluations, image-segmentation results, and the appendix VQA experiment (Tables 1–5).

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main-text experiments and the VQA and segmentation evaluations in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 3.1–3.4 retain identical cyclic archive optimization, elite sampling, model-merging crossover, SVD mutation, and final aggregation. The VQA adaptation in Appendix A.1.5 also matches.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same coding, AgentBench DB/OS, language/generalization, TextVQA, and four image-segmentation task datasets. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same fine-tuning and merging comparators, including gradient-based merging, CMA-ES, and NSGA-II, plus the base-model and GPT comparisons. Comparator membership also matches throughout Tables 2–5.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, few-shot settings, the 1,200-generation budget, and segmentation training/evaluation protocols are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same cyclic-QD, mutation, and sampling ablations. Generation/archive analyses in Figures 5–6 and segmentation similarity and error analyses in Table 4 and Figures 7–8 are also identical.

E5.justification: Run information and statistical reporting are unchanged. Both retain the same point estimates without seed-based uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries, rankings, plots, and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 reports CycleQD MBPP/DB/OS scores of 76.4/38.2/42.6, averaging 52.4, in both versions; Appendix Table 5 retains its VQA score of 54.1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for sampling, crossover, mutation, aggregation, and model similarity are identical. No assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about skill acquisition, baseline superiority, GPT-3.5 comparability, language retention, and applicability to image segmentation.

C2.justification: Explanations of QD diversity, mutation effects, and expert compatibility remain identical. Limitations involving divergent experts, computational cost, and segmentation failures are retained without revision.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same optimizer, learning rates, batch sizes, epochs, CycleQD hyperparameters, dataset preparation, H100 hardware, and training-time disclosures. The code-access link and its destination also match.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix B, in-text citations, and the reference list are unchanged. The relationships to prior QD, model-merging, and LLM-agent research remain identical.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025.' The arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 27 November 2024 to v3 dated 27 January 2025. Body wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–5, captions, placement, and body layout are unchanged. Rendered page bodies are pixel-identical after excluding the publication header and arXiv stamp.

improvement.justification: Only publication and version markings change. The methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations, reproducibility information, and body presentation, including both appendices, are identical. These administrative updates do not materially improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
